description: Council of Cooperative Health Insurance (CCHI) mandatory coverage requirements for all cooperative health insurance policies issued in Saudi Arabia. Based on CCHI Resolution No. (37) of 2018 and the Implementing Regulations of the Cooperative Health Insurance Law (Royal Decree M/10 dated 01/05/1420 AH). All policies must meet the Minimum Benefits package. Non-compliant exclusions or copay structures are void.

clauses.title: Mandatory Inpatient Hospital Coverage
clauses.full_text: All cooperative health insurance policies must cover inpatient hospitalisation including room and board (general ward minimum), surgical and medical procedures, anaesthesia, ICU and CCU care, nursing services, diagnostic investigations, blood and blood products, and prescribed medications during admission. Pre-authorisation is required for all elective inpatient admissions. Emergency inpatient admissions may not be denied for lack of prior authorisation. Maximum copayment for inpatient admission is SAR 100 per day with an annual cap of SAR 3,000 per member.
clauses.regulatory_note: CCHI Resolution No. (37) 2018 — Mandatory Benefits Schedule, Article 3

clauses.title: Mandatory Outpatient Coverage
clauses.full_text: Outpatient coverage for general practitioner visits, specialist consultations, diagnostic laboratory tests, and basic radiology is mandatory for all CCHI-approved health insurance policies. The maximum copayment for outpatient services is 20% of the eligible amount, not to exceed SAR 100 per visit. Dental and optical outpatient services may be excluded from the minimum benefits but must be clearly stated in the policy schedule. Follow-up visits within 30 days of an inpatient discharge for the same condition must be covered at no additional copayment.
clauses.regulatory_note: CCHI Implementing Regulations, Article 18 — Minimum outpatient benefits

clauses.title: Mandatory Emergency Treatment — Saudi Arabia and Worldwide
clauses.full_text: Emergency medical treatment must be covered at any licensed facility within Saudi Arabia without prior authorisation. Emergency treatment outside Saudi Arabia must be covered up to SAR 100,000 per incident with post-notification within 48 hours of admission. No copayment may be applied to emergency services within Saudi Arabia. Insurers may not deny emergency claims on pre-authorisation grounds. Stabilisation and transfer costs for emergency cases must be included.
clauses.regulatory_note: CCHI Resolution No. (37) 2018, Article 5 — Emergency services mandate

clauses.title: Mandatory Maternity Coverage
clauses.full_text: Health insurance policies in KSA must cover maternity benefits for female insured members including normal vaginal delivery (SAR 8,000 minimum), caesarean section (SAR 12,000 minimum), antenatal consultations (minimum 6 visits covered), postnatal care (2 visits), and complications of pregnancy. Maternity waiting period must not exceed 12 months from first effective date. Newborn care for the first 30 days is covered under the mother's policy. Complications arising from pregnancy including gestational diabetes and pre-eclampsia may not be excluded.

clauses.title: Mandatory Pharmaceutical Coverage
clauses.full_text: Prescribed medications for covered conditions must be reimbursed under all CCHI-compliant policies. Generic medications must be covered at 100% (no copay). Brand-name medications may be subject to a maximum copay of 20% up to SAR 50 per prescription. Medications prescribed during inpatient stays must be covered in full with no copay. Chronic disease medications (diabetes, hypertension, asthma, thyroid) must be covered up to SAR 10,000 per member per year. The formulary must include all medications on the Saudi FDA approved list for EBP conditions.

clauses.title: Minimum Annual Benefit Limit
clauses.full_text: All CCHI-approved health insurance policies must provide a minimum annual benefit limit of SAR 500,000 (five hundred thousand Saudi Riyals) per insured member per policy year for the mandatory minimum benefits package. This limit applies regardless of the number of claims made. Policies providing less than SAR 500,000 annual coverage are non-compliant. Premium policies may offer higher limits. Sub-limits for individual benefit categories must not reduce coverage below: Emergency per incident: SAR 100,000; Inpatient per admission: SAR 100,000; Maternity: SAR 12,000.
clauses.regulatory_note: CCHI Implementing Regulations, Article 9 — Annual benefit thresholds

clauses.title: CCHI Copayment Caps — Maximum Permitted
clauses.full_text: The following copayment caps apply to all CCHI-regulated policies and may not be exceeded: Outpatient visits (GP and Specialist): 20% of eligible claim, maximum SAR 100 per visit. Inpatient admissions: SAR 100 per day, annual maximum SAR 3,000. Emergency treatment (KSA): SAR 0 (prohibited). Pharmacy (brand): 20%, max SAR 50 per prescription. Diagnostics and laboratory: 20%, max SAR 100 per visit. Physiotherapy: 20% per session. Annual out-of-pocket maximum for mandatory benefits: SAR 10,000 per member per policy year. Policies imposing higher copays are non-compliant and the excess amount is unenforceable.
clauses.regulatory_note: CCHI Resolution No. (37) 2018, Annex 1 — Standard copay schedule

clauses.title: Mandatory Waiting Period Caps
clauses.full_text: CCHI regulations restrict waiting periods as follows: Initial waiting period for all illness claims (not accident): maximum 30 days from policy effective date. Pre-existing disease (PED) waiting period: maximum 12 months for the basic plan (Iqama holders). Maternity waiting period: maximum 12 months from first coverage date. Specific disease waiting period (joint replacement, hernia, cataract): maximum 12 months. Accidents have zero waiting period from day 1 of coverage. Emergency conditions have zero waiting period. Insurers may offer shorter waiting periods but may not impose longer ones than these caps.
clauses.regulatory_note: CCHI Implementing Regulations, Article 12 — Waiting period restrictions

clauses.title: Prohibited Exclusions — Conditions CCHI Insurers May Not Exclude
clauses.full_text: The following conditions and services may not be excluded from CCHI-compliant policies: (a) Emergency medical treatment at any facility in KSA; (b) Maternity complications (pre-eclampsia, gestational diabetes, placenta previa); (c) Newborn care for first 30 days from birth; (d) HIV/AIDS treatment for legal Iqama-holding residents — basic treatment must be covered; (e) Chronic disease management (diabetes, hypertension, asthma, thyroid) — medications and monitoring; (f) Dialysis for end-stage renal disease; (g) Cancer treatment including chemotherapy and radiotherapy (up to the annual limit); (h) Mental health acute inpatient treatment — up to 7 days per year. Any policy clause purporting to exclude these categories is void under CCHI regulations.
clauses.regulatory_note: CCHI Resolution No. (37) 2018, Article 6 — Non-excludable conditions

clauses.title: Pre-Authorisation Requirements and Prohibitions
clauses.full_text: Pre-authorisation is required for all elective inpatient admissions and daycare procedures in KSA. Insurers must respond to pre-authorisation requests within: Emergency within 1 hour (phone), Urgent within 4 hours, Elective within 24 hours (business days). Insurers may not deny pre-authorisation solely due to administrative non-compliance if the medical necessity is established. Pre-authorisation may not be required for: any emergency admission, follow-up outpatient visits for same condition within 30 days of discharge, chronic disease monitoring consultations, and preventive screenings. Refusal to grant pre-authorisation must be communicated in writing with clinical grounds stated.
clauses.regulatory_note: CCHI Regulations, Article 21 — Pre-authorisation process and timelines
